newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S DELTA SAYS NO GM DEAL IMMINENT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S DELTA SAYS NO GM DEAL IMMINENT.

text.p: South African car maker Delta Motor Corp said on Tuesday that any prospective tie-up with U.S. giant General Motors Corp (GM) was still far from finalised.
The firm announced late in January that it was currently engaged in talks with GM on potential areas of increased cooperation.

But a company spokesman told Reuters that the discussions were still ongoing. "There is a process of discussion taking place, but there is no result at present and probably not for some time to come," he said.
Speculation has focused on the idea that GM will take a stake in Delta, following similar recent moves by Japanese firms Toyota and Nissan .
GM's U.S. rivals Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp have already returned to the country, following disinvestment during the apartheid era.
The spokesman confirmed that GM taking a stake was an option being pursued, but that there are other possibilities too. "(A stake) is one thing we are looking at," he said.

Delta produces cars originally designed by GM's Adam Opel AG unit in Germany. GM and Delta also in 1995 formed a joint venture in Port Elizabeth to make leather seat covers for export to Opel in Europe.
GM's Delphi Packard Electric unit also owns a 50.1 percent interest in South Africa's largest vehicle wiring harness maker, Auto Cable Industries Pty Ltd.
